Historical release evidence

Version-specific release verification records and the limits of that evidence.

On this page
01 Current release evidence

These are version-specific evidence records and procedures, not a claim that every later build was tested. For current installed readiness, run gateway rollout --verify --json. Return to the verification overview.

Current release evidence

The v0.2.23 gateway removes generated agent roles, worker defaults, role CLI commands, task prompt text, and the injected title tool. All 528 source tests pass. Client agent settings and user-authored role files survive unchanged even when an obsolete gateway policy exists. Native naming and caller tools remain ordinary client operations. The real signed SDK passes eight Responses cases with 13 mock requests and no paid inference. A caller base-instruction marker reaches the upstream in the same developer message bytes on every request. The SDK requires a string instruction-template field in custom model metadata; the gateway supplies an empty string. Missing or null templates are rejected before inference. Existing executors retain loaded settings until normal retirement; their role files must remain available until they finish.

The v0.2.22 installed fixture passes eight cases using the original signed SDK and 13 mock upstream requests. Genuine interrupted responses preserve incomplete message status and continue under the original acknowledged user-turn ID. A completed caller tool executes once, and its result reaches the continuation once. Unfinished tools never dispatch. Minimal completed responses with an ID and no status are accepted. Clean pre-output EOF retries once; text or completed tool output prevents replay and retains a failed terminal. The SDK can execute an already completed caller tool before a later stream failure; the fixture records that execution rather than claiming that failure undoes it. Isolated configuration remains unchanged, authentication is not copied, and all owned SDK processes and RPC timers stop. All 528 source tests pass. There are no paid inference calls. These checks establish translation and safe recovery, not the upstream cause of the reported live EOF or successful activation in an older running daemon.

The v0.2.21 work reproduces the separate-process ownership gap with the original signed SDK: a second process reads an active native chat as interrupted and cannot Stop its real owner. A shared native owner passes 18 mock checks through stdio and Unix. Both clients read the actual running turn; Stop, owner-client disconnect, reconnect steering, history, warm approval replay, and follow-up complete through that same owner. Gateway sharing remains independently selectable. Its installed combined-owner fixture passes 20 checks, including another client reading and stopping the actual active gateway turn. All 508 source tests pass. No paid requests, copied authentication, or native configuration edits occur in those isolated fixtures.

Gateway administration also passes real signed SDK checks. Metadata probes use transient non-originating clients, leave frontend identity intact, never answer its approval, and permit SDK idle unload after unsubscribe. These tests establish backend ownership; they do not establish the reported viewer state or rendered cloud behavior.

The separate gateway-only SDK passes four real upstream compaction regressions and 44 installed stdio, Unix, and shared checks. Selected-model compaction, model switches, provider failure/retry, Stop, active steering, goal budgets, follow-up, and saved-history resume retain the original user turn's ACK ID. Actual extracted desktop handlers retain association in both ACK arrival orders. The installed SDK also passes all 41 Fast checks with Standard defaults. Installer verification includes repeated installation under a prefix containing spaces and quotes. These use mock upstreams and do not establish rendered desktop or cloud transport behavior. Older running apps and services require guarded activation.

The v0.2.20 silent-stop work passes 446 Node tests. Eight native-exit regressions verify that real buffered completions drain before exit classification, genuine unfinished executor exits emit errors before shutdown, and intentional close remains bounded. The signed SDK continuation fixture verifies actual end_turn values, assistant phases, nested final output, and exactly-once tool dispatch. It uses a mock upstream, unchanged isolated native configuration, and no copied authentication or paid inference.

The immutable v0.2.20 preflight installer passed repeated installation and all four continuation scenarios with the signed SDK. Its existing Fast fixture also passes all 41 checks. Native relay tests pass 15 cases in the release profile, including continuous-output fairness, reconnect ownership, bounded teardown, stderr privacy, and failed diagnostic writes. Installation and tests do not activate the new code in older running components.

The supplied native MacBook 2 example continued producing reasoning events without renderable summaries during a five-minute quiet period. Its original turn later interrupted, another completed, and a new turn started. The reported idle-looking viewer has not been captured on that exact chat, so its cause is unverified. Native execution bypasses the gateway's Responses translator; the continuation fix is not attributed to that native incident.

An isolated replay of the installed desktop's actual observer handlers also shows that an inserted manual compaction turn can bind a pending user bubble to the compaction ID instead of the later user-turn ID. Backend compaction success therefore does not establish desktop association or full UI parity. The verified v0.2.21 gateway-only SDK avoids that preceding manual turn; older packages retain the legacy limitation. Rendered desktop checks remain separate from the fixtures.

The v0.2.19 legacy compaction work reproduces the pinned SDK's previous-model downshift failure, then verifies recovery with the selected gateway model. Its source gate passes 425 tests. The immutable installer passed repeated installation, including a prefix containing spaces and quotes, and 38 signed SDK compaction checks across stdio and Unix/WebSocket. The checks cover short and long switches, reasoning effort, real completion ordering, two interruptions, selected-provider failure, persisted failed-state recovery after reconnect, proof replay, and safe shared ownership refusals. They use 67 mock requests and zero paid inference; fixture process groups and provider timers finish at zero.

The same installer passed all 41 existing signed SDK Fast checks with 36 mock requests. These fixtures preserve native configuration and copy no authentication. They do not establish rendered controls, live subscription compaction, or the built-in cloud transport. Recovery requires an idle per-connection executor with no active goal. Shared execution requires explicit compaction because the SDK has no atomic idle admission operation. Installation preserves running apps and older loaded adapters; existing connections need activation before using the fix.

The v0.2.18 speed work retains the secondary account's declared Fast capabilities for seven of its eight models; Daybreak offers none. All eight aliases retain their routes and Standard defaults. The four selected Copilot models expose no selected-model speed tier. Direct Copilot Fast requests fail before CLI startup.

The real secondary registration completed priority inference through the public Responses resource, but the provider reported service_tier: "default". A raw fast request was rejected, so the Codex adapter normalizes that alias to priority. The normalized adapter request also completed as Standard. These results prove authentication, forwarding, and truthful completion metadata; they do not prove accelerated inference for this subscription route.

The signed SDK fixture verifies local stdio and Unix WebSocket speed controls against a mock upstream. It covers saved defaults, explicit Standard, temporary turn tiers, forks, loaded versus cold resume, and another client choosing Standard. The native Fast flag remains false while private gateway executors can request priority. No subscription inference, primary configuration, authentication copy, rendered desktop control, or built-in cloud transport is involved in that fixture. The source gate passes 355 tests, including delayed notifications, timestamp ties, stale snapshots, revision ABA, and request-start ordering fences. The final immutable v0.2.18 installer passed repeated installation and all 41 signed SDK checks across both transports, with 36 mock upstream requests and zero paid inference. All fixture processes were stopped afterward.

Release installation preserves open apps and services. The running primary inference host and older connected-machine adapters need coordinated activation before these new speed fields reach their existing desktop connections.

The October 12 retired-feature audit found none of the three obsolete settings in the primary Mac, MacBook Pro 2, or Studio native configuration, including profiles. MacBook Pro 2's five gateway engine snapshots and Studio's one snapshot were also clean. No configuration edits were required. Historical warning records remain historical; Guardian feedback telemetry is not deprecated configuration.

v0.2.17 closes two remaining argument paths: metadata SDK preflight and shared execution requests from older adapters. Its gate passed 264 tests. A signed SDK metadata proof supplied all three retired CLI flags with native hooks=false and hooks=true. Neither SDK spawn received a retired key, neither emitted a matching warning, and both returned their original hooks value. The proof used only initialization, configuration reads, and model listing; no inference or copied authentication. Native and isolated configuration bytes were unchanged.

The v0.2.16 installed preflight passed 260 tests and a real launchd cleanup fixture. Staging one future startup entry preserved the old PIDs. Manual promotion and promotion with an old relay still loaded were refused. The actual primary launchd process then promoted the plan after the fixture jobs unloaded. Responsibilities and native configuration, installation, enrollment metadata, and signed app identity were unchanged. All fixture jobs were removed afterward; no provider inference or native authentication was used.

The October 12 login audit found five gateway-owned startup files on the primary Mac (desktop setup, inference, and three required tunnels), two on Studio (desktop setup and native relay), and one unified job on MacBook Pro 2. The two primary-Mac Login Items named gateway corresponded to desktop setup and inference. Next-login consolidation preserves both duties in one registration. macOS's cached background-item history is distinct from scheduled startup files.

The audited catalog contains 36 models: 11 native models and 25 added routes. The added routes comprise 12 Claude models, eight Codex 2 models, four Copilot models, and one local Qwen model. Qwen advertises text input only. Discovery and catalog presence do not establish inference access for every model. The four Copilot routes are GPT-6.1-Sol, GPT-5.6-Terra, Sonnet 5, and Opus 5.5.

The October 12 audit found MacBook Pro 2's running desktop adapter and native relay on v0.2.8 under one supervised gateway service, with the v0.2.14 command installed. Shared executors had not been activated. The running relay retained the machine's original environment and installation IDs. The primary Mac's inference process was upgraded to v0.2.14 during the stream-failure investigation.

The real Claude CLI then reported a rejected five_hour window with reset 2026-10-12T17:10:00Z, followed by assistant.error: rate_limit and an erroneous result with subtype: success. This established a subscription limit for that failure, rather than a tool or transport failure. v0.2.15 preserves those native discriminants and reports the window and provider reset time. Its installed preflight passed 244 tests and a signed SDK fixture: precise quota failure, reset timestamp in the SDK error, and successful continuation in the same chat after simulated provider recovery. No real provider requests or copied native authentication were used in that fixture. Tests also cover persisted observations, authenticated remote reads, expired data, and preservation of the primary usage response. Rendering the added Claude usage row remains a separate desktop check.

Studio's v0.2.11 relay is connected using its original environment and installation IDs. Its fresh app-server catalog includes Claude, Codex 2, Copilot, and Qwen. Its rendered original-connection picker and inference remain unverified. The primary Mac still needs native relay activation and checks through its original connection. Do not remove a working SSH connection before its native replacement passes those checks.

MacBook Pro 2 stream failures

The primary daemon logged repeated Codex 2 GPT-6.1-Sol failures after roughly three to six seconds, well before its ten-minute deadline. The archived 257-item conversation replayed successfully against the secondary account with and without internal metadata and synthetic item IDs. Those results do not identify the cause of the live failures; the older log discarded upstream failure metadata.

The v0.2.12 candidate queues up to 32 waiting requests behind the configured provider concurrency and retains safe upstream stream-failure diagnostics. Tests verify a 30-request burst, FIFO admission, waiting cancellation and deadlines, bounded capacity, and one transient server-error retry before any output. Partial responses and quota failures are never retried. These backend checks do not prove that every existing connected chat is stable.

A replay with the archived desktop tool catalog reproduced upstream server_is_overloaded in about four seconds. Later full-catalog replays completed, so that catalog is not a deterministic failure trigger. The installed v0.2.12 daemon passed a 30-request mock burst with four running providers and 26 waiting requests. Its signed SDK recovered from a mock transient error with one retry. Live MacBook Pro 2 tests through the existing forward to that daemon passed Codex 2 reads, edits, follow-ups, reasoning, interruption, and recovery. Shared production health contained unrelated chats, so its global active count cannot prove cleanup of one particular request.

The v0.2.13 candidate loads Claude's private virtual MCP catalog before inference and records fixed categories for rejected calls. Its isolated live Claude Opus 5.5 test passed streaming, the hidden AGENTS.md marker, file reads and edits, follow-ups, reasoning progress, interruption, zero active requests after cleanup, and recovery through the signed SDK. The cause of the earlier live Claude call rejections remains unconfirmed; the new categories preserve evidence for another occurrence. These results do not replace rendered desktop or prolonged stability checks through the original connection.

After v0.2.13 activation, Edi's affected connected chat still failed. Its safe diagnostic classified the Claude call as unknown_tool, rather than duplicate IDs or malformed input. Small live file loops therefore did not reproduce that remaining failure. The v0.2.14 candidate replaces per-request numbered MCP names with stable caller identities, translates replayed call/result names, and accepts only exact or unambiguous current-catalog aliases. It canonicalizes Codex's plain tools and explicit functions namespace using the pinned SDK's default namespace. Foreign tools and stale numeric bindings remain invalid.

Tests cover reordered and filtered catalogs, namespace defaults, ambiguous local names, and preservation of arguments, call IDs, results, and input messages. A live Claude test retained a real caller result across reordered catalogs and different forced tool choices without executing any caller action. The exact rejected name from the original failure was not logged, so the affected native chat still needs its own confirmation after activation.

The primary Mac's native config.toml still matches the digest recorded before activation. Gateway preferences are stored separately. Native Codex and user actions can change settings on the other Macs, including project trust; their current files do not establish byte-for-byte identity with earlier snapshots. The isolated backend tests below check that the adapter leaves their native configuration unchanged during each run.

The remaining desktop checks are:

Check Evidence Gap
Model selection and refresh The native connection returns the combined catalog. Backend config and catalog defaults agree. Confirm Refresh preserves the selected gateway model and effort in the primary Mac's UI.
Claude files and images User-driven Claude checks wrote the release-check seed and CLAUDE_NATIVE_OK on MacBook Pro 2 and read a code supplied only in an attached image. Repeat follow-up and saved-chat recovery through the original connection.
Codex 2 follow-up Backend and Unix proxy checks passed file edits and retained image history. The native release-check proof has no Codex 2 completion marker.
Stop and recovery Backend checks passed interruption and recovery. The native relay logged interruption requests. Establish which provider handled each interrupted cloud turn and verify its recovery.
Qwen The real backend tool loop passed and the model appears in the combined catalog. Verify text, file tools, follow-up, and interruption through the original connection.
Reasoning controls v0.2.8 persists all six display efforts. MacBook Pro 2's local rendered Claude menu showed Max. The user also confirmed that all levels now appear on the primary Mac. Capture the primary Mac's menu and verify refresh persistence when using the connected computer.
Auto-review reviewer A fake-gateway run of the pinned SDK sent the reviewer request as codex-auto-review (low effort, strict JSON schema), and the route and catalog tests cover routing and advertisement. The route is on by default for every Auto-review approval. The subscription endpoint accepting that slug was not called live: the stored login had expired, and refreshing it would rotate the installed credential. Run a browser action in a Claude chat and confirm that Auto-review items appear and the action completes (node_repl).

Shared execution ownership and outage recovery passed the v0.2.10 backend gate. The signed SDK checks below prove gateway ownership across several adapter clients in an isolated development fixture. The v0.2.10 CLI is installed on the test Mac; its GitHub release remains a draft and its adapter changes are not activated. Native executors still have separate ownership in each adapter, and the installed release's cloud connections have not passed the corresponding checks.
